description: Per-stage master table: selects the level packages and map-local presentation for a battle/menu stage, including its display-text key, nested map effect and decal asset lists, character lighting/material grading, global effect/decal/blood colors, stage-select and mini-map textures, mission-layout IDs, reverb and ambient sound, and sequencer lighting/bloom overrides.

ID.technical: FName primary key/import key (native Id, export label ID); the lookup name, not normally a value read from the row. Status_FindMapRow returns the first row named Id in MapDataTables (DTM +0x3A0); sources include GameManager.StudioBattleLevelRequest_CA0.BattleLevel, DomainExpansion/StoryMission/Script/RoomPlacement Id_Map, hard-coded SDM_10/20/30/40, VLM_01 and CharacterCapture. Reads of the value forward MapRow->Id to BattleWidget -> HUD -> Radar SetMiniMap, key SequencerLightDataTables via FindSequencerLightRow(MapId, File->Filename), key SequencerCapture MapOverrideCaptureSource, and identify stage-select/random-map choices. MAP_00 is a synthetic UGameStageSelectWidget row, not a table row. Export has 30 unique rows: MAP_01..MAP_16 (including MAP_14_01/MAP_15_01), DEM_01..03, VLM_01, SDM_10..40, SRM_10..30 and CharacterCapture.

Id_MapText.simple: Glossary text id for the stage name.
Id_MapText.technical: FName text key such as GLS_NAME_MAP_01 (export values are GLS_NAME_* keys, not localized strings). UI consumers pass it straight to SetTextIdOnly (stage-select item and focused stage) or store it as the option label in FreeBattleRuleSelect's Id -> text StageOptions map. GameCharacterSelectWidget looks up a Map row to label the selected stage; GameShopSaleItemListItemDataBase returns it as the map-name label and falls back to ERROR when no row is found. UGameStageSelectWidget's synthetic MAP_00 row hard-codes GLS_NAME_MAP_00. DEM/VLM/SDM/SRM/CharacterCapture rows have their own GLS_NAME_* ids.

Filename.simple: Ordered list of level packages that make up the map.
Filename.technical: TArray<FName> (native FileName, row +0x18; constructor default empty). StartBattleLevelPreload and FStudioBattleSystem2D0::RequestStageLevels call RequestStreamLevel on each name without an IsNone guard. Most phase transitions either call PhaseTrans_RequestLevels(..., MapRow->FileName, ...) or copy the array into StudioRequestedLevelNames_F8 for the phase mailbox. Story helpers append StoryRoomPlacement.LevelDesignName after the map levels, return the list for a Script row, and Story_PrepareBattleRequest unguardedly copies the active map's array. Exported arrays are 4 names: base map, *_Environment, *_LevelDesign and an optional foliage/battle-area level or None; the CharacterCapture row contains only CharacterCapture.

Id_MapEffect.simple: Foreign key to the map's effect asset list.
Id_MapEffect.technical: FName; when non-None, BattleAssets_MapEffects_12BD820 resolves it in MapEffectDataTables (DTM +0x3B0) and appends the nested MapEffect row's FileName list to an Effect primary-asset loader batch. StartBattleAssetPreload uses StudioMapEffectLoaders_180; GamePhase_BattleBase uses StudioMapEffectLoaders_720. NAME_None and a missing row yield no effects. Export values are MAP_05, MAP_06, MAP_09, MAP_11, MAP_12, MAP_13, MAP_14, MAP_15 and MAP_16; every other row is None.

Id_MapDecal.simple: Foreign key to the map's decal asset list.
Id_MapDecal.technical: FName; when non-None, BattleAssets_MapDecals_12BD690 resolves it in MapDecalDataTables (DTM +0x3C0) and appends the nested MapDecal row's FileName list to a Decal primary-asset loader batch (StudioMapDecalLoaders_1D0 in preload, _770 in BattleBase). NAME_None and a missing row yield no decals. Export values are MAP_01, MAP_03, MAP_06, MAP_07 and MAP_13; all other rows are None.

CharacterLightColor.technical: FVector (row +0x38; constructor default ZeroVector). UGameActorMaterialController::ApplyMapCharacterLighting pushes it as material vector parameter 'Character Light Color'; AGameEffectManager::ApplyMapColors pushes the same vector to the world's MaterialParameterCollection instance as 'FXLightColor'. The lighting call fans out to every managed character's character/weapon/shikigami controllers, and sequencer evaluate paths apply it to the bound character, NPC, level object, shikigami or weapon; sequencer point lights use it as FLinearColor when a map row is selected. Character-capture actors use the CharacterCapture map row here and retain this parameter even though widget Common parameters later override shadow/grade parameters.

CharacterOverlayColor.technical: FVector (constructor default ZeroVector). Its sole traced consumer is UGameActorMaterialController::ApplyMapCharacterLighting, which sets the material vector parameter 'Character Light OverlayColor' on character, weapon and shikigami material controllers (including sequencer-bound targets and the CharacterCapture map row for capture actors). It is not one of the parameters overwritten later by FGameWidgetCharacterCaptureCommonParameter.

CharacterShadowColor.technical: FVector (row +0x68; constructor default ZeroVector). ApplyMapCharacterLighting sets material vector parameter 'Character Light ShadowColor'; ApplyMapColors writes it to the MaterialParameterCollection parameter 'FXCharacterColor'. Capture actors first receive the CharacterCapture map row's value, then GameCharacterCaptureActor and AbramsSequencerSceneCaptureActor overwrite 'Character Light ShadowColor' with FGameWidgetCharacterCaptureCommonParameter.CharacterLightShadowColor (widget-capture data, not this table). Export values vary per map.

CharacterContrast.technical: float (constructor default 0.0f). ApplyMapCharacterLighting sets scalar parameter 'Character Contrast' through the shared material controller; the fan-out reaches all managed characters' character/weapon/shikigami controllers and sequencer targets. For character capture the CharacterCapture map row supplies the initial value, after which the widget's FGameWidgetCharacterCaptureCommonParameter.CharacterContrast overrides it (default 1.0 in that struct). Export values include 0.9 (MAP_06) and 1.0 for most stages.

CharacterSaturation.technical: float (constructor default 0.0f). Written as scalar parameter 'Character Saturation' by UGameActorMaterialController::ApplyMapCharacterLighting for every managed character/weapon/shikigami and sequencer-bound target. The CharacterCapture row value is initially applied to capture actors and then overwritten by FGameWidgetCharacterCaptureCommonParameter.CharacterSaturation (widget default 0.0). Export values range from -0.316 to 0.12.

CharacterLevelsWhite.technical: float (constructor default 0.0f). ApplyMapCharacterLighting sets scalar parameter 'Character LevelsWhite' on the character/weapon/shikigami controllers of managed and sequencer-bound actors. Capture actors get the CharacterCapture row's value first, then FGameWidgetCharacterCaptureCommonParameter.CharacterLevelsWhite (widget default 1.0) overwrites it. Export values include 0.8 (MAP_04) and 1.0 for most stages.

CharacterLevelsMiddle.technical: float (constructor default 0.0f). ApplyMapCharacterLighting sets scalar parameter 'Character LevelsMiddle' across managed characters, their weapons/shikigami and sequencer-bound targets. Capture actors' initial map-row value is overwritten by FGameWidgetCharacterCaptureCommonParameter.CharacterLevelsMiddle (widget default 1.0). Export values include 0.85 (MAP_01), 0.88 (MAP_05) and 0.9 (MAP_06).

CharacterLevelsBlack.technical: float (constructor default 0.0f). ApplyMapCharacterLighting sets scalar parameter 'Character LevelsBlack' through the same material-controller fan-out as the other grading fields. Character capture first applies the CharacterCapture map row, then FGameWidgetCharacterCaptureCommonParameter.CharacterLevelsBlack (widget default 1.0) overwrites it. Export values include 0.45 (MAP_06) and 1.9 on one row, with many stages at 1.0.

EffectColor.technical: FVector (row +0x98; constructor default ZeroVector). AGameEffectManager::ApplyMapColors writes it to the world's MaterialParameterCollection instance as vector parameter 'Color'. ApplyMapColors is called from battle phase setup/results, battle states 05/07/08/10 and the studio level-sequencer cast spawn. This is distinct from FGameDataTableRow_MapGround.EffectColor, which AbramsSequencerSetEffectGroundColorEvaluate reads after a physical-surface trace. Export values include (1,1,1) and per-map tints such as MAP_01 (0.88,1,1) and DEM_02 (0.67,0.8,1).

DecalColor.technical: FVector (row +0xB0; constructor default ZeroVector). AGameEffectManager::ApplyMapColors writes it verbatim to the MaterialParameterCollection vector parameter 'DecalColor' alongside Color/FXCharacterColor/FXLightColor/BloodColor, using the same row selected by the battle or sequencer phase. Export values are dark per-map tints, e.g. MAP_01 (0.18,0.23,0.30).

BloodColor.technical: FVector (row +0xC8; constructor default ZeroVector). AGameEffectManager::ApplyMapColors writes it to the world's MaterialParameterCollection as 'BloodColor'. No separate sequencer or ground-surface field with this name is consumed; the row comes from the active BattleLevel or the studio sequencer's cached map row. Export is (1,1,1) for 29 rows and a single non-white row.

SequencerBloomIntensityOffset.simple: Bloom multiplier applied by sequencer post-process tracks.
SequencerBloomIntensityOffset.technical: float (constructor default 0.0f). FAbramsSequencerCopyPostProcessVolumeEvaluate reads it from MapModule->GetMapRow() (sequencer-manager row first, then BattleLevel row). Values nearly equal to 1.0 skip the write. Otherwise the target volume's copied BloomIntensity (CachedValueA) is compared: if the current value equals CachedValueB it is reset to CachedValueA * Scale (then B is updated); if it still equals A nothing happens; otherwise the current value is multiplied in place. OnSetup zeroes A/B; OnPreExecute copies the source volume's settings and initializes both to the copied bloom. Export values are 1.0 except 0.4 on MAP_14, MAP_14_01, MAP_16 and DEM_03.

MapSelectPlacementIndex.simple: Non-negative marks a stage as selectable in stage UI.
MapSelectPlacementIndex.technical: int32 (row +0xE4; constructor default 0). Every traced consumer only tests the sign: stage-select list, free-battle stage options, main-menu free-battle/PvE/PvP icon preloads and Story_PickRandomMapId keep rows with index >= 0 and skip negative ones. No consumer in the reconstructed source uses the numeric value as an array index or sort key; StageItemParameterMap is keyed by Id instead. Export indices are 0..11 for selectable MAP_ rows and -1 for MAP_14_01, MAP_15_01, DEM_*, VLM_01, SDM_*, SRM_* and CharacterCapture. UGameStageSelectWidget's synthetic MAP_00 row is hard-coded to 0.

MapSelectIconFileName.technical: FName (row +0xE8; default empty). Consumers add it to WidgetTexture primary-asset loader batches or call FindDynamicLoadTexture and set it as a brush/texture parameter. Main-menu FreeBattle/PvE/PvP and FreeBattleRuleSelect gate loading on MapSelectPlacementIndex >= 0; IntervalPvE and WidgetTest preload every row's icon; BattleSettingsBackgroundWidget, BattleSituationOverviewWidget, FreeBattleWidget, StageSelectWidget and StoryCharacterSelectWidget display it. Some callers fall back to hard-coded T_UI_Common_StageImage_MAP_00 for the synthetic MAP_00/random-stage case. Export is a T_UI_Common_StageImage_* name for selectable maps, T_UI_Lobby_* for VLM_01 and None for DEM_02/03, SDM_*, SRM_* and CharacterCapture.

MiniMapFileName.simple: Mini-map texture name shown in battle HUD.
MiniMapFileName.technical: FName (row +0xF0; default empty). GamePhase_BattleBase preloads the active map's value (retail unguarded) and also the map referenced by each character's DomainExpansion row; BattleAssets_DomainExpansionMiniMap performs the same nested CharacterSpecialAttack -> DomainExpansion -> Map join. UGameBattleRadarWidget::SetMiniMap resolves MapRow->Id, checks the name is not None, looks up the preloaded widget texture and sets the dynamic material's 'MiniMapTexture' parameter; missing row/texture leaves the old material. Export values are T_UI_MiniMap_* for MAP/DEM rows and None for VLM_01, SDM_*, SRM_* and CharacterCapture.

Id_MissionLayout.simple: Mission-layout ids indexed by the current wave.
Id_MissionLayout.technical: TArray<FName> (default empty; 16 slots in every exported row). AGameBattleManager::GetCharacterStartTransform uses the active MissionWave->MissionLayoutIndex: if MapRow->Id_MissionLayout is valid at that index and the entry is not None, it resolves the id in MissionLayoutDataTables (DTM +0x9B0) and overrides the start transform's translation/rotation from Layout.Location[Index] / Layout.Rotation[Index] (each guarded by IsValidIndex). The final Z is then ground-traced, so the layout's Z is not authoritative. Export ids use per-map ST/DLC01 and PVE00..PVE05 naming, with None filling unused slots; story-only maps are all None.

ReverbRate.simple: Reverb bus send amount for the stage.
ReverbRate.technical: float (row +0x108; constructor default 0.0f). GameBattle_ApplyStageMapRow and its inlined copies, battle phases/states and the studio level-sequencer cast spawn assign it to AGameSoundManager::ReverbBusSendLevel (+0x398). Every voice/SE player later receives Player->SetBusSendLevelByName(ReverbBusName, ReverbBusSendLevel), with ReverbBusName defaulting to 'Reverb'. Transition paths explicitly reset the manager value to 0 when leaving battle/sequencer stages. Export values are 0.0, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.15.

Id_SoundEffect.simple: Ambient background sound id for the stage.
Id_SoundEffect.technical: FName (row +0x10C; default empty). AGameBattleManager::PlayMapAmbientSe resolves it with Status_FindSoundEffectRow(SoundEffectDataTables DTM +0x730, bCheckNone=true) and calls GameSoundManager.PlayAmbientSe(Row->CueSheetName, Row->CueName, GameSoundDefaultPlayParameter); a missing row/None plays nothing. StartMapAmbientSe first prefers the map referenced by the finish target's DomainExpansion row and otherwise uses the active BattleLevel row. GameBattle_ApplyStageMapRow and battle states 07/08 call PlayMapAmbientSe after applying colors/reverb. Export values are SE_BG_* for MAP/DEM/VLM rows and None for SDM_*, SRM_* and CharacterCapture.

notes: MapDataTable is registered as primary asset name 'MapDataTable' in AGameDataTableManager::StartInitialLoading and resolved into MapDataTables (DTM +0x3A0) after all loaders complete. Status_FindMapRow returns the first table holding the row; the export contains a single table with 30 unique rows. Retail RVAs quoted in the reconstructed source are static-analysis provenance, not runtime verification.

Row selection is context-dependent: the common key is GameManager.StudioBattleLevelRequest_CA0.BattleLevel, but domain expansions, story missions/scripts/room placements and level-sequence ids select named rows instead. AGameSequencerManager caches a pointer in MapRow (+0xCB8) via SetMapRow (cleared by ResetSequencer); UAbramsSequencerMapDataModule::GetMapRow falls back to the BattleLevel lookup. MAP_00 is a synthetic stage-select row, not data.

GameBattle_ApplyStageMapRow is the shared battle hand-out: ApplyMapCharacterLighting, ApplyMapColors, SetMapRow, SetBattleLevelRequest(MapRow->Id), ReverbRate and PlayMapAmbientSe. Battle states 05/07/08/10 and battle phases contain inlined variants; for domain expansions, state 07 switches between the caster's DomainExpansion.Id_Map and the active battle level depending on bFinished.

ApplyMapCharacterLighting fans out through AGameCharacterManager to every managed character and then through character/weapon/shikigami controllers to their material controllers; sequencer SetMapColor can apply the same row to a bound character, NPC, sequencer level object, shikigami or weapon, caching AppliedMapRow by the EGameSequencerMapDataType channel (1 = current map, other values = enum-name row lookup). OnTearDown reapplies the current map's row.

Character-capture actors explicitly look up the 'CharacterCapture' row for lighting; their widget Common parameter struct subsequently overwrites CharacterLightShadowColor and all five scalar grade parameters, so only CharacterLightColor/OverlayColor from the map row remain authoritative at capture time. No launch or network was used; all statuses come from static consumer traces and the available export.

MapDataTable's colors/levels are per-stage and global/material-parameter based. They are distinct from MapGroundDataTable, whose surface-keyed rows drive footstep/bound effects and the sequencer's ground-color trace. Vector component fields (X/Y/Z) are omitted here because the renderer inherits the parent FVector annotation.

usages.detail: Resolves MapDataTable into MapDataTables (+0x3A0) once all primary-asset loaders finish; registration is at line 336.
Status_FindMapRow: first row with the requested Id in any Map table, with optional None check.
Starts streaming every Filename level for the requested BattleLevel; also kicks off Id_MapEffect and Id_MapDecal nested asset preloads.
Id_MapDecal -> MapDecalDataTables -> FileName list; Id_MapEffect -> MapEffectDataTables -> FileName list at line 280.
Writes all three Character* colors and five Character* scalar grades to material parameters; reached through character/weapon/shikigami/level-object controllers.
ApplyMapColors writes EffectColor, CharacterShadowColor, CharacterLightColor, DecalColor and BloodColor into the world's MaterialParameterCollection instance.
Shared stage-row hand-out combines lighting, colors, sequencer cache, HUD map id, reverb and ambient SE.
Domain-expansion flow chooses DomainExpansion.Id_Map before finishing and the active BattleLevel afterwards.
MissionWave.MissionLayoutIndex indexes Id_MissionLayout; the resolved MissionLayout row overrides character start location/rotation before ground tracing.
PlayMapAmbientSe resolves Id_SoundEffect against SoundEffectDataTables and plays its cue as ambient SE.
Battle system streams Filename packages and swaps the stream-level set when the map changes.
PhaseTrans_RequestLevels copies a map row's Filename array and phase request into the next phase's transition state.
Preloads the map icon for a character's DomainExpansion map and the active map's MiniMapFileName; line 519 applies colors and reverb.
Studio cast spawn finds the BattleLevel row, applies colors and lighting, caches it in the sequencer manager and reads ReverbRate.
SetMapRow caches the row pointer (+0xCB8); line 1227 joins MapRow->Id with SequencerLightDataTables via current file parameter.
Sequencer map-row provider: cached sequencer row first, then a MapDataTables lookup of the BattleLevel name.
Byte channel selects current map (1) or an EGameSequencerMapDataType enum-named row; ApplyMapColor fans the row out to the bound actor's material controller.
Reads SequencerBloomIntensityOffset and applies the deduplicating multiply to the copied post-process volume's BloomIntensity.
MapDataId 0 uses custom RGB values, 1 uses the current map row, and larger values look up an enum-named row; CharacterLightColor becomes the point light color.
Uses MapRow->Id as the key for per-map capture-source overrides in the sequencer section.
Builds the stage list from rows with MapSelectPlacementIndex >= 0, keys extras by Id, and appends a synthetic MAP_00 entry.
Stage options use Id_MapText as the label and MapSelectPlacementIndex as the selectability filter.
Resolves the HUD's map id and applies MiniMapFileName's preloaded texture to the minimap material.
Capture actors use the CharacterCapture map row for lighting; widget Common parameters later override the shadow/grade fields.
Story room placement levels append LevelDesignName to Map->FileName; script levels and random-map selection are at lines 354 and 362.
Hard-codes SDM_10/20/30/40 Map rows for four story level sequences and passes them to Sequencer.SetMapRow.
